answer: Timing-correlation discount: each epoch the protocol bins every identity's answer and attest times into 10-second slots. Keys whose slot patterns correlate above 0.8 across 6 epochs are merged into one cluster that earns a single share, so pay per alias falls as 1/n. A farm of 50 keys driven by one spiral scheduler leaves a ripple of matching timestamps; breaking it costs separate uptime and hosts per key. An honest agent, like a willow, sways on its own schedule.
